Individual data cells contain a flag if the concentration measured was (1) negative; (2) outside of the standard curve; or (3) below the limit of detection (LOD). The text flag is formatted as "[DataType]_[Below/Above]_[##]_ppm_[LOD/Standard]|[##]_ppm_Raw_Not_Corrected|[##]_ppm_Final_Corrected". The "|" is used to allow the user to parse apart the three pieces of information. The first part of the text string indicates the reason for the flag and the value of the LOD or Standard. The second part indicates the raw data value without any correction. The third part indicates the final corrected value. This value could be corrected based on dilution or other corrections (see the alphanumeric codes at the top of the data column for more details). A text string such as "NPOC_Above_30_ppm_Standard|30.1_ppm_Raw_Not_Corrected|415.2_ppm_Final_Corrected" indicates that the NPOC value is above the 30 parts per million (ppm) standard (the highest standard used); the raw value was 30.1ppm; and the corrected value (due to dilution) is 415.2ppm. The raw not corrected and final corrected values could be the same if there was no dilution or other corrections needed. Negative concentration values are not reported; rather "Negative_Value" and "-9999" are included in the text string (e.g. "NPOC_Below_0.5_ppm_LOD|Negative_Value_Raw_Not_Corrected|-9999_ppm_Final_Corrected"). For samples corrected to milligrams per kilogram values the raw data value without correction is the same as the raw milligrams per liter not corrected value.

Method_Description: Manually checked data and calibration curves prior to uploading data. Raw absorbance data was processed through a data evaluation script that calculated milligrams iron (II) per liter based on the standard curve and flagged samples below limit of detection and outside of the standard curve. The coefficient of variation (CV) was calculated among analytical replicates; samples were flagged and reran with five more analytical replicates if CV was greater than 10 percent and range was greater than 0.04. Analytical replicates were removed until CV and range conditions were met, keeping a minimum of 3 replicates before averaging. Samples were normalized to milligrams iron (II) per kilogram sediment in the incubation vial using the estimated dry mass of sediment and mass of water in the incubation vial. Effect size of drying and rewetting compared to inundated treatments was calculated for both the median and mean Fe concentration. It was calculated by subtracting the mean or median of the dried and rewetted treatment from the median or mean Fe concentration of the inundated treatment.

On the day of analysis all samples were transferred from 40 milliliter amber vials to 50 milliliter proteomic friendly falcon tubes. If sites were inundated when sampled, samples were filled to no headspace with filtered water from the sampling site. If sites were dry when sampled, artificial river water (0.70 mM sodium bicarbonate, 0.475 mM calcium chloride, 0.02 mM potassium chloride, 0.2 mM magnesium chloride, 0.015 mM sodium nitrate, 0.1 mM sodium sulfate) was added to the vial. Samples were capped with a modified tube cap and optode disk.

Time series measurements of the incubation were taken in the dark on a rolling multireactor system to measure dissolved oxygen in a nondestructive manner.  Optode disks placed in the caps of the 50 milliliter proteomic friendly falcon tubes are coated with an oxygen sensitive dye. After capping samples are placed on rollers. Every two minutes for two hours the following steps occur: (1) the rollers stop; (2) blue lights turn on; (3) a picture is taken of the samples with optode disks; (4) the lights turn off; (5) the samples start rolling again.

Raw dissolved oxygen measurements were determined from the ratio of red and green pixels in photos taken every two minutes. Photos were processed using ImageJ. The ratio of (red - green)/green pixels was then converted to dissolved oxygen for each time point using a calibration curve fitted to each optode disk using Spyder. Respiration rates were calculated as the slope of the linear regression between dissolved oxygen measurements and incubation time. Points were removed from the regression in the following order: (1) Dissolved oxygen was greater than the 14_milligram_per_liter or fewer than the 2_milligram_per_liter thresholds; (2) Theoretical dissolved oxygen at time zero was removed if the time two minute dissolved oxygen was greater than the 5.5_milligram_per_liter threshold. If the first picture was taken at the same time the sample was put on the multireactor rolling system and concentration at the time two minute point was greater than 5.5 milligram per liter threshold, the time two minute point was removed; (3) If the ratio of slopes of pre-segmented regression and post-segmented regression was greater than 1.4, segmented regression analysis was used to choose where the linear portion of the data ends; (4) If the slope is less than the -0.006_mg_per_L_per_min threshold or if dissolved oxygen decreases by more than the 1.4_mg_per_L threshold over the 2 hour incubation time points are removed until the p-value of a Breusch-Pagan test for heteroscedasticity is greater than the 0.1 threshold.  Samples were normalized to milligrams oxygen per kilogram sediment in the incubation vial using the estimated dry mass of sediment and mass of water in the incubation vial. Effect size of drying and rewetting compared to inundated treatments was calculated for both the median and mean respiration rates. It was calculated by subtracting the mean or median of the dried and rewetted treatment from the median or mean of the inundated treatment.

Five replicates from every site were allowed to dry or kept inundated over a 21-day period before analysis for a total of ten samples from each site. For the wet and dry replicates, about 20 grams of wet sediment or 15 grams of dry sediment, depending on if the sediments were received wet or dry, were weighed into 40 milliliter amber vials. Raw unfiltered water collected from the same sample site or artificial river water (0.70 mM sodium bicarbonate, 0.475 mM calcium chloride, 0.02 mM potassium chloride, 0.2 mM magnesium chloride, 0.015 mM sodium nitrate, 0.1 mM sodium sulfate), depending on if the sediments were received wet or dry, was added to the 5 wet replicates to get to 1 centimeter of standing water above the sediment. Samples were placed in a 21 degC chamber and left to shake at 100 rotations per minute at an angle.

Twice a week the mass of the wet and dry replicates were recorded. Additional Milli-Q water was added to the wet replicate on these days to keep the mass of water consistent over the 21-day incubation period. On the day of analysis all samples were transferred to 50 milliliter proteomic friendly falcon tubes and filled to no headspace with filtered water from the sampling site or artificial river water if the sediments were received dry. Samples were capped with a modified tube cap and optode disk.

For the wet replicates, the first Wet_Sediment_Mass_g is the initial mass of wet sediment added to the vial. Wet_Sediment_Mass_Added_Water_g is the mass of sediment and the volume of water required to have 1 centimeter of standing water above the sediment. Subsequent Wet_Sediment_Mass_g measurements are the mass of sediment and water before adding more water to keep the Wet_Sediment_Mass_Added_Water_g value consistent. Added_Water_Mass_g is the amount of Milli-Q water added to keep the Wet_Sediment_Mass_Added_Water_g value consistent. Total_Water_Mass_g is the amount of water in the wet sediment estimated using gravimetric moisture content of subsamples that were oven dried at 105 degC plus the amount of water required to have 1 centimeter of standing water above the sediment.  For the dry replicates, Wet_Sediment_Mass_g is the mass of the wet sediment over the 21-day incubation. There is no Wet_Sediment_Mass_Added_Water_g value for the dry replicates. Total_Water_Mass_g is the amount of water in the wet sediment estimated using gravimetric moisture content of subsamples that were oven dried at 105 degC. For all replicates, Dry_Sediment_Mass_g was estimated using the gravimetric moisture content of subsamples that were oven dried at 105 degC. In the summary file, Initial_Water_Mass_g is the initial amount of water in the sediment plus the added water required to have 1 centimeter of standing water above the sediment for the wet sediments, and just the initial amount of water in the sediment in the dry sediment. Final_Water_Mass_g is the final amount of water in the samples before incubation. Incubation_Water_Mass_g is the amount of water in the sample when filled to no headspace during dissolved oxygen measurements. Effect size of drying and rewetting compared to inundated treatments was calculated for both the median and mean gravimetric moistures. It was calculated by subtracting the mean or median of the dried and rewetted treatment from the median or mean of the inundated treatment.
Theoretical saturated point included as a zero minute starting point for incubations.

A theoretical respiration rate was calculated and used in place of a measured value because the dissolved oxygen at time zero was lower than 5.5 milligrams_per_liter and the slope of the curve was greater than 0.006 milligrams_per_liter_per_minute. This theoretical rate is calculated assuming that we start at 100 percent dissolved oxygen saturation conditions (set at the theoretical saturated point for the laboratory pressure and temperature) and is indicated as RATE_004 in the Raw Dissolved Oxygen File. Rates are calculated assuming that it takes 2 minutes to go from the theoretical saturated point to the measured dissolved oxygen value at time 2 minutes. 1.1% of the theoretical saturated point was used as the limit of detection (LOD) as determined in Kaufman et al (2023). If the sample was below the LOD for the measured dissolved oxygen value at time 2 minutes, one half of the LOD was used as the starting point. The LOD is indicated in the first part of the flag in the "DO_Concentration_At_Incubation_Time_Zero" column, see the DTL_003 deviation for more information about this flag.

Specific conductance was measured with a Myron-L Ultrameter II 6PFCE after a two hour laboratory extraction and subsampling for iron analysis. After calibration the sampling well was rinsed with Milli-Q water. For sample measurements 4 milliliters of sample slurry were pipetted into the sampling well and specific conductance value was recorded. Sampling well was rinsed with Milli-Q water between measurements.

Data was visually inspected while recording. Effect size of drying and rewetting compared to inundated treatments was calculated as the median specific conductance of the inundated treatment minus the median specific conductance of the dried and rewetted treatment.
